test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Two coils, A and B, such that A is connected to a battery through a key and B is connected to a galvanometer, are arranged parallel and close to each other. During which of the following duration will the phenomenon of electromagnetic induction be observed?

(a) Two minutes after closing the key.

(b) During the interval the key is taken out.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (b)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electromagnetic induction** is observed when there is a **change in the magnetic flux** linked with a coil.
 
• In the given scenario, electromagnetic induction will not occur two minutes after closing the key because the system would have reached a steady state by then.
 
• However, during the interval when the key is taken out, there is a change in the current through coil A, which changes the magnetic flux linked with coil B, thus inducing a current in coil B.
 
• Therefore, the phenomenon of electromagnetic induction is observed **only during the interval the key is taken out**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic induction** was discovered by **Michael Faraday** and is described by **Faraday's Law of Induction**.
 
• Faraday's Law states that the induced electromotive force in any closed circuit is equal to the rate of change of the magnetic flux through the circuit.
 
• This principle is the working mechanism behind many electrical devices such as transformers, inductors, and many types of electrical generators and motors.
 
• The direction of the induced current is given by** Lenz's Law**, which states that the induced current will flow in such a direction as to oppose the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
 
• This phenomenon is crucial in the functioning of various technologies, including power generation and electromagnetic braking systems.
